subject: Conditional trial top-up and mutually bound commitment — NexaHealth RFP
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah@nexahq.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: RFP trial usage and potential top-up

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the integration looked promising for our clinical QA pipeline. We’ve been running a short side-by-side and wanted to share preliminary usage: attached is a CSV with calls and token counts for Jun–Nov. Early signal is that Redwood’s latency consistency is a differentiator for our team.

Two asks as we move toward the vendor selection call next Wednesday:
- Would Redwood consider a conditional trial top-up to cover an increased eval window (additional 1.2M tokens) if we commit to a 12-month reserved capacity evaluation by Jan 15?
- Can you share a short escrow-style agreement that outlines the credit allocation and expiration so we can show Procurement?

I’m looping in Tom from Procurement on next steps. Looking forward to a quick yes/no so we can finalize the shortlist.

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
Head of ML, NexaHealth
[sent from mobile]

Attachment: nexa_trial_usage_JunNov.csv (csv)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah@nexahq.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: RFP trial usage and potential top-up

Hi Sarah — great to see the usage shape, thanks for sending.

Short answer: yes, we can support a conditional top-up. Proposed approach (to keep procurement comfortable and protect both sides):
1) Redwood will provide a 1.2M-token credit top-up as a one-time allocation for the RFP evaluation.
2) Top-up is conditional on NexaHealth signing a mutually bound 12-month evaluation commitment letter by 2027-01-15. Commitment terms are light — reserved capacity + minimum monthly usage metric — we’ll share a template.
3) Credits will be placed in an escrow-like agreement and expire 60 days after activation if no reserved capacity order is placed.

Next steps I suggest:
- Ben will draft the credit escrow agreement (doc attached as a working draft).
- Karthik will run the cost modeling for the reserved capacity commitment to confirm the price band for Nexa’s expected throughput.

Tom — happy to jump on a 20-min procurement call to walk through safeguards. If this sounds reasonable, I’ll push Ben’s draft and Karthik’s pricing by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | https://www.redwood.com

Attachment: credit-escrow-agreement-draft.docx (Word)

From: Tom Reed <procurement@nexahq.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sarah Liu <sarah@nexahq.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: RFP trial usage and potential top-up

Marissa,

Procurement’s main concerns are enforceability and accounting treatment. A couple quick asks: 
- Can the escrow agreement include a simple trigger clause (activation on first API call after agreement) and an audit right for Nexa?
- Will the credits be recognized as a prepaid expense on our books, or do they look like marketing/promotional credits? This affects our GL coding — we prefer PREPAID (capex/expense deferral) treatment.

If you can confirm those points, I’ll expedite internal approval.

Regards,
Tom Reed
Procurement Manager, NexaHealth

Subject: Internal: Nexa — credit escrow draft and accounting notes

Folks — following Tom’s procurement points, attached is the agreed working draft of the credit escrow plus an internal note on recognition. Highlights: 
- Activation trigger: first API call after signed commitment or sooner if Nexa signs an activation addendum.
- Expiry: 60 days after activation unless a reserved order is placed.
- Accounting guidance: treated as deferred revenue / prepaid credit (Finance prefers PREPAID until drawn). That should satisfy Nexa’s GL ask.
- Legal: small redlines suggested around audit window and data retention; Vanessa can own legal redline loop.

Marissa — if you’re OK with this version, I’ll send to Tom and Sarah with a short cover note and the signed mutual commitment template (they can sign electronically). Karthik, attach the price band and call volumes so we can be specific about the reserved capacity metric.
